data.narrative:
Machina Labs is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $80M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable across the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and Nimble Robotics at similar or adjacent stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $80M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B step-ups to the next stage, yielding $152M. The peer-median method examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.0B to $1.8B, producing a median implied valuation of $1.6B. The peer set reflects the capital intensity and growth trajectory characteristic of frontier manufacturing automation.

These methods produce a triangulated range of $129M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $888M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Machina Labs' relative position within the peer cohort. Key variables driving valuation outcomes include the company's revenue run rate and growth trajectory relative to Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B) and Dexterity ($1.6B), near-term market adoption of its core technology, and capital efficiency metrics relative to adjacent-stage companies. Additional clarity on customer concentration and path to profitability would narrow this range materially.
